title: Microcap response modes — proto pad
content:
Purpose / problem statement:
Quick sketch for an MVP that gives apps fine-grained controls over token budgets per response and a small set of response "modes" (concise / default / expanded) with automatic graceful expansion when quality metrics justify additional tokens. Goal: allow product teams to bound per-request spend in hosted mode while keeping UX good for high-value flows.

Why this exists (context):
- Customers are building chat and assistive UIs and need predictable per-interaction cost bands (finance, legal).
- Current options are coarse (max_tokens) and need manual tuning per prompt; they cause either clipped answers or unexpectedly high bill spikes.
- We can provide a higher-level primitive: "microcap modes" + soft expansion policy that surfaces tradeoffs and automates safe expansion.

High-level concept (MVP):
- Expose response_mode param on API: one of [concise, balanced, expanded]. Default balanced.
- Each mode maps to a nominal token cap and a soft budget multiplier (e.g., concise=cap 80, mult 1.0; balanced=cap 256, mult 1.25; expanded=cap 1024, mult 1.5).
- Soft expansion: if model detects low confidence / hallucination risk / fails safety check, runtime can request +N tokens up to cap * multiplier with a trace reason. Client sees final token usage and a reason code.
- Fallbacks: when reaching hard absolute cap or quota, system returns truncated answer plus a compressed summary + redirect hint (e.g., "ask to expand" flow).

User stories (rough):
- As a product manager I want a mode toggle so I can give free users concise replies and pay customers expanded replies so I can control cost per cohort.
- As a developer I want predictable 95p token usage for my "quick-reply" route so I can budget monthly spend.
- As a platform engineer I want telemetry hooks for expansion events so I can monitor quality vs cost tradeoffs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API accepts response_mode param; docs show mapping to nominal caps.
- Runtime emits event when soft expansion is applied with reason tag.
- Client receives final token_count and expansion_trace in response metadata.
- Default behavior must never exceed user's hard_limit header (explicit opt-in to allow multipliers).
- E2E test: for sample prompts, concise mode uses <= 90 tokens 95% of time; balanced <= 320 tokens 95% of time.

API sketch (developer-facing):
POST /v1/responses
body: { "model": "rwd-7b-compressed", "input": "...", "response_mode": "concise", "hard_token_limit": 400 }
Response metadata (headers/body): { "x-token-used": 128, "x-expansion-applied": "true", "x-expansion-reason": "low_confidence_answer_fragment", "x-final-mode": "balanced" }
Notes: hard_token_limit overrides any multiplier, runtime should validate and fail-fast if request wants multiplier > 1 and hard limit would be exceeded.

UX/Console ideas:
- Route-level default mode toggle in Console with per-key overrides.
- Dashboard panel: "Expansion events" that shows percent of responses that upgraded, average cost delta, and quality metric (BLEU/QA pass rate) where available.
- Quick rule editor: "If expansion increases predicted quality > X% allow up to multiplier Y" (future).

Observability / metrics to capture:
- expansion_applied_count, expansion_rate_per_route, avg_token_delta, pct_exceeding_nominal_cap, total_cost_delta_by_mode, quality_gain_by_expansion (via eval set).

Experiment plan (short):
1) Internal sim: run 50k historical requests through offline predictor that estimates whether expansion would change answer fidelity. Tune multipliers so that expansion_rate ~ 2-8% for balanced.
2) Canary: enable for 1 internal team, console toggle, route-level only. Collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
3) Gate: if expansion improves eval QA pass by >= 7% and cost delta < 12% then widen to public.

Open questions / risks:
- How do we reliably detect "low confidence" in a way model-agnostic? (logit gap? calibration head? separate verifier model?)
- Billing UX: expanded responses increase tokens after-the-fact; should we surface an "estimate" pre-flight? Need billing contract decisions.
- Abusive loops: apps could intentionally craft prompts to trigger expansions; need quota/guardrails.
- Storage/trace size: expansion_trace adds metadata overhead; is it significant?
- Interaction with streaming: how to pause streaming to decide expansion? Or stream until cap then optionally continue if expanded.

Implementation notes (engineering rough):
- Runtime hook point: after generation finishes and safety/quality checks run, evaluate expansion predicate with a fast verifier; expansion requires allocating more output tokens and re-running decoder from KV cache (should be efficient).
- Fallbacks: precompute compressed summary algorithm (extractive compress) to deliver minimal useful text when hard cap hit.
- Telemetry: cheap boolean tag and token delta metric emitted per request.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with billing/legal on post-facto token billing model (owner: Finance).
- Quick prototype: wire response_mode to existing max_tokens + naive multiplier in hosted runtime (owner: Daniel C, target: 2 week spike).
- Create offline simulation job to estimate expansion benefit on internal eval corpora (owner: Mira S).
- Draft Console toggle mockups and sample copy for admin docs (owner: Aisha R).

Notes to self (random ideas):
- Could offer "explainable expansion": when expanded, include which prompt sentences triggered the expansion and a short confidence delta so PMs can audit.
- Tiered billing label: show expanded tokens separately in invoices so customers can opt into expanded mode at higher plan.
- Consider tiny local verifier that runs cheaply on CPU to avoid adding large GPU cost to decision path.

Quick sample flow (for product demo):
User asks: "Summarize the latest quarterly report and recommend 3 action items."
- concise: 3–4 bullets, 50–80 tokens, cost band A.
- balanced: standard summary + 3 bullets, 200–300 tokens, cost band B.
- balanced with expansion: model initially returns an underspecified answer; verifier detects low confidence -> runtime requests +150 tokens -> final answer is more robust (expansion_trace included).

End of proto pad. This is intentionally light — want to iterate with eng on the verifier and runtime cost model before writing a formal PRD.
